mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the periods following a sustained GDP decline, or if the correlation between GDP decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which leads to increased economic activity and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy and inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it signals a strengthening labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand side, which leads to increased economic activity and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the periods following a sustained increase in housing starts, or if the correlation between housing starts increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real final sales (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% in a month and industrial production (INDPRO) is stable or increasing, it signals a robust supply side and healthy demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of RSAFS increase and stable/increasing INDPRO on positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
